title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: What Are Embeddings — Vector Representation of Text
summary: Embeddings are dense, fixed-dimensional numerical vectors that represent the semantic meaning of text in a continuous geometric space.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Embeddings are dense, fixed-dimensional numerical vectors that represent the semantic meaning of text in a continuous geometric space. A well-trained embedding model maps semantically similar texts to nearby points in this space — "canine" and "dog" become close vectors, while "dog" and "automobile" are far apart. In RAG, embeddings are the bridge between human language and mathematical retrieval: documents are pre-embedded and stored in a vector database; at query time, the query is embedded and the nearest document vectors are retrieved. The embedding space has geometric properties: direction encodes meaning (king - man + woman ≈ queen), magnitude is often normalized away, and clusters form around semantic topics. The quality of embeddings directly determines the upper bound of retrieval quality — no retrieval strategy can recover from a bad embedding model.

quiz.explanation: Modern embedding models are trained with contrastive learning: given a query and a set of candidates, the model learns to maximize similarity between the query and its positive (relevant) document while minimizing similarity with negative (irrelevant) documents. The loss function is typically InfoNCE (used in CLIP, SimCSE) or MultipleNegativesRankingLoss (used in sentence-transformers).

quiz.question: What is embedding dimensionality and how does it affect RAG performance?
options: Instruction-tuned embeddings (like BAAI/bge-large with Instruct prefix, or E5-mistral-7b-instruct) accept a task-specific instruction prefix that guides the embedding…
MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across 8 task categories (retrieval, reranking, classification, clustering, STS, etc.) on 56 datasets.
Don't rely solely on MTEB public benchmarks — they may not reflect your domain.
Dimensionality is the size of the vector produced by an embedding model (e.g., 768, 1536, 3072).
quiz.explanation: Dimensionality is the size of the vector produced by an embedding model (e.g., 768, 1536, 3072). Higher dimensions: can capture more nuanced semantic distinctions, but increase storage cost (2x dimensions = 2x memory and disk), indexing time, and retrieval latency. Lower dimensions: faster and cheaper, but may lose semantic nuance.

options: Root Cause: Old documents embedded with model-A (768d), new queries embedded with model-B (1536d) — different vector spaces, similarity meaningless.

quiz.explanation: Instruction-tuned embeddings (like BAAI/bge-large with Instruct prefix, or E5-mistral-7b-instruct) accept a task-specific instruction prefix that guides the embedding toward the desired representation. For example: "Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: {query}" vs just "{query}". The instruction shifts the embedding distribution toward what's needed for retrieval vs clustering vs classification.

quiz.explanation: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across 8 task categories (retrieval, reranking, classification, clustering, STS, etc.) on 56 datasets. For RAG, the retrieval subtask (BEIR benchmark) is most relevant — it tests embedding-based document retrieval on NFCORPUS, TREC-COVID, HotpotQA, etc. A model scoring high on BEIR retrieval tasks will generally perform well in RAG pipelines.
